column2: Confirm a booking over the website's surface
column3:

- The website shows a booking as confirmed only after the ledger has recorded it. (AC1)
- A confirmation the ledger rejects shows as failed, never as confirmed. (AC2)

- A call to CON-001 without a valid service token is refused at the Platform gateway. (AC4)

column2: Write confirmed bookings to FERRYMASTER
column3:
Acceptance criteria:
- Booking sends BKHOLD, BKCONF, BKAMND and BKCANC in the format CON-006 documents, and the FERRYMASTER test region accepts each one in the weekly end-to-end run. (AC1)
- When FERRYMASTER rejects a write or does not answer, Booking retries and the booking keeps its hold. No channel sees `confirmed` until FERRYMASTER has accepted. (AC2)
- The same write sent twice is applied once in FERRYMASTER. (AC3)
- p95 ledger write latency in the weekly end-to-end run is no worse than the 2.1 s measured for UNK-001. (AC4)
- Booking's contract tests run against the ledger simulator with no connection to FERRYMASTER. (AC5)

column2: Hold a seat and release it when it runs out
column3:
Acceptance criteria:
- A channel that asks to hold a seat through CON-001 gets back a booking reference and an expiry time, and no other channel can sell that seat until the hold ends. (AC1)
- A failed or abandoned payment releases the hold, and the seat is available to every channel again. (AC2)
- A hold that isn't confirmed in time is released, and Booking publishes a state-changed event. (AC3)

What this story relies on:
Written without the vault, so what this story relies on is named by ID only: CAP-014.FR1, CAP-014.FR2.

Open for the design:
- Open for `tech-design-grill`: whether a hold survives a restart of the Hold keeper. The design says only that holds live in Redis.
Conflicts:
- Conflict with an epic criterion: EPC-031.AC4 says a hold ends when payment fails; the design lets a hold run to its expiry. The story follows the design and the conflict goes upstream.

column2: Amend and cancel online
column3:
Acceptance criteria:
- A customer can change the date or time of a crossing on the website and sees the re-quoted fare before they accept it. (AC1)
- A customer can cancel a booking on the website, and every channel shows it as `canceled` once FERRYMASTER has accepted the cancellation. (AC2)
- A change that is not allowed is refused with a reason the channel can show the customer, and nothing reaches FERRYMASTER. (AC3)
